standard.title: Text structure, purpose and hybrid genres
standard.description: explain how texts are structured depending on their purpose and how language features vary, recognising that some texts are hybrids that combine different genres or elements of different genres
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can understand how different text types are structured to achieve different purposes and identify how language features vary across text types (AC9E7LA03). They have not yet examined how texts combine multiple genre structures or analysed hybrid texts that deliberately blend conventions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain how text structures serve specific purposes and how language features vary accordingly, including recognising and explaining hybrid texts that combine elements from different genres.

nodes.label: Structure and language features serve purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how the structural choices and language features of a specific text type are designed to achieve its communicative purpose.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how the structure and at least two language features of one text type (e.g. critical response, exposition) work together to achieve its purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Explain how texts such as critical responses, expositions, interpretations, discussions, literary recounts and memoirs are structured and how their language features serve their communicative purposes, with attention to how placement of images and written text may vary in print vs online formats.
wider: Compare two texts with similar purposes but different structures (e.g. a written exposition vs a formal speech) and explain how structural variation affects meaning
Examine how formal speeches use structure and language features differently from written argument to achieve persuasive effect with a live audience
Analyse how the placement of images and written text in non-linear online texts (e.g. news websites) creates different reading pathways and affects the text's purpose

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a working repertoire of text types and their conventions. Encountering a range of text structures — not just one — builds the comparative lens needed for the hybrid genre concept at node 2.

success_criteria: Names the purpose of a given text and identifies at least two structural or language features that serve that purpose.
Explains why those features are suited to the text's purpose rather than simply labelling them.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires students to recognise that two genre conventions are being combined in a hybrid text — which requires knowing what those conventions are in the first place. Students who have not built a working repertoire of distinct text-type conventions cannot identify what is being hybridised.

nodes.label: Hybrid genres
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and explain how hybrid texts combine elements from different genres, identifying what purposes or effects this combination achieves.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify that one provided text combines elements from two different genres and explain what effect this combination creates for a reader.
nodes.typical_width: Recognise and explain hybrid texts that deliberately combine genre elements — such as a narrative that embeds exposition, or an opinion piece that uses memoir structure — explaining how the combination serves the text's overall purpose.
wider: Analyse how a specific hybrid text (e.g. creative nonfiction, a personal essay, a docudrama) exploits the conventions of multiple genres to position the reader in complex ways
Investigate how digital and multimodal texts (e.g. interactive journalism, video essays) create new hybrid forms by combining text, image, audio and structural elements from different genres
Create a short hybrid text that deliberately combines elements from two genres and annotate the structural and language choices made

response_modes.reason: The concept of 'hybrid genre' is non-obvious — students expect texts to be cleanly categorisable. Encountering a range of hybrid examples (memoir-as-argument, narrative nonfiction, docudrama) dissolves the expectation of clean genre categories and builds the flexible reading lens the descriptor requires.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Hybrid texts are increasingly prevalent in contemporary digital media and creative nonfiction. The range of hybrid forms available — personal essay, narrative journalism, video essay, interactive documentary — offers rich comparative analysis opportunities for advancing students.
success_criteria: Identifies specific elements from two different genres present in one hybrid text.
Explains how the combination of genre elements serves a purpose or creates an effect that neither genre alone would achieve.
